newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine business urges exchange rate review.
newsitem.headline: Philippine business urges exchange rate review.

text.p: Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista said on Monday the private sector had urged for a review of the governments' foreign exchange policy to raise the competitiveness of exports.
Bautista said a demand for the review was made by businessmen when they met President Fidel Ramos and key economic officials last Friday.

In a paper presented to Ramos, the businessmen said: "the exchange rate should be reviewed to allow gradual adjustments to a more realistic rate through a possible gradual depreciation of the peso in a well-calibrated manner to attain competiveness in the global market.."

"He (President Ramos) generally agreed with the principle that a peso-dollar exchange rate should be competitive with Philippine products, but said that this should be determined by market forces," Bautista said.
Bautista saidf the President referred the matter to the Central Bank, which is independent of the executive branch.
The Philippine peso has been subject to speculation that it may be the next target after last week's de facto devaluation of the Thai baht.
On Monday, the Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate to 30 percent from 24 to protect the peso against a fresh round of attacks.
